professional.subject: The Monday reporting pack
professional.body:
Hi,

The services page says weekly client reports are still assembled in spreadsheets, and the homepage describes a Monday leadership pack copied out of three systems. That is a lot of manual work for a 12-person team.

A short conversation could map which of those sources should refresh on a schedule, and which numbers need a single definition before anyone automates them.

Worth a 15-minute chat?

{{sender_name}}

conversational.subject: Monday's pack, three systems
conversational.body:
Hi,

I was reading how Northwind runs weekly client reports. They are still assembled in spreadsheets, and a Monday leadership pack is copied out of three systems. That sounds like the work that quietly eats a small team's week.

I am curious which of those three sources is the painful one. If it is useful, I can share how I would decide what to refresh on a schedule and what still needs a person to explain it.

Open to a 15-minute chat?

{{sender_name}}

bold.subject: Stop copying the Monday pack
bold.body:
Hi,

Northwind's services page still has weekly client reports assembled in spreadsheets, and the Monday leadership pack is copied out of three systems. A 12-person consultancy should not spend its best hours on that copy step.

The fix is not another dashboard no one trusts. It is one definition per metric, and a refresh that does the copying.

Worth 15 minutes to see if that is actually the bottleneck?

{{sender_name}}

consultative.subject: Which number gets copied?
consultative.body:
Hi,

Northwind helps manufacturers trust their numbers, and the site is frank about the messy middle: weekly client reports assembled in spreadsheets, and a Monday leadership pack copied out of three systems.

Before automating any of that, I would want to know which source changes the decision and which metric definitions still disagree. That is the conversation I would like to have.

Would a 15-minute working session be useful?

{{sender_name}}
